issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor removes outer Delimited() and regresses multi-clause alterations in a single statement
issues.detail: Replacing Delimited(OneOf(...)) with bare OneOf(...) means statements like 'ALTER TABLE t ADD col_b ... , DROP COLUMN col_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS col_c' (valid T-SQL per MS docs and previously covered) no longer parse. The PR labels this 'invalid' but the removed fixture is taken from Microsoft documentation. Restore multi-clause support or justify the change.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no justification, no test, and beyond MS docs
issues.detail: The CREATE LOGIN grammar adds NumericLiteralSegment as a valid DEFAULT_LANGUAGE value, but MS docs specify a language name/alias (sysname) and no fixture exercises the numeric form. The PR description does not justify this widening. Either remove the alternative or add a fixture demonstrating documented use.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar over-accepts signs on increment and lacks coverage
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is added before both numeric literals, permitting '+' signs and standalone sign tokens (and possibly whitespace between sign and digits) on the increment. T-SQL accepts negative seeds but the sign handling is too loose, and no fixture exercises the increment-sign branch. Tighten to a minus-only or merged signed-literal grammar and add a negative-increment test.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT grammar makes the CONSTRAINT keyword optional inside the Delimited list
issues.detail: The inner Sequence wraps CONSTRAINT (plus IF EXISTS) as optional, so 'ALTER TABLE t DROP a, b' parses with no CONSTRAINT keyword at all, which is invalid T-SQL. The keyword should be required at least once per clause to disambiguate from DROP COLUMN and prevent silent acceptance of malformed input.

issues.description: New declare_table_type.sql fixture omits trailing semicolon, inconsistent with the rest of the file
issues.detail: The added 'declare @var table (... INDEX ...)' block lacks the terminating semicolon that every other statement in the file uses. Not a parse error, but inconsistent style and could mask statement-terminator emission in batch parsing. Add the semicolon to match conventions.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR adds useful T-SQL parser coverage (table-variable indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative IDENTITY seeds, multi-DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT) but contains one clear regression and several permissiveness gaps. All six reviewers flag the AlterTableStatementSegment refactor: removing the outer Delimited() drops support for multi-clause ALTER TABLE statements that are valid per Microsoft documentation, and the corresponding fixture was deleted rather than preserved. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting NumericLiteralSegment and the over-permissive IdentityGrammar (signs on both seed and increment, no negative-increment test) are also unanimously called out. Minor concerns include DROP CONSTRAINT making the CONSTRAINT keyword optional within a delimited list and a stylistic inconsistency in the new declare_table_type fixture. The ALTER TABLE change should be reverted or justified before merge.
